extracted.intended_audience: students and mathematicians at various career stages (primary school through postdoc); especially undergraduates, graduate students, and postdocs
extracted.subtask_description: A collection of practical career and professional-development advice for mathematicians at different stages (primary school, high school, undergraduate, graduate, postdoc), covering research habits, learning strategy, presentation, and career decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic disclaimer — tailor advice to your situation
rubrics_metrics.description: The advice here is very generic in nature; you will need to evaluate many factors, contexts, and needs specific to your own situation before making important career decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss major decisions with your advisor (if you have one) because they know your situation; use common sense; do not treat this as a one-size-fits-all formula.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work hard and professionally
rubrics_metrics.description: It is important to work hard, and work professionally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine diligence with professional habits (meeting deadlines, clear communication). This is paired with also finding ways to enjoy your work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enjoy your work
rubrics_metrics.description: It is also important to enjoy your work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sustained research careers require intrinsic enjoyment; balance professional rigor with activities that keep you motivated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Think ahead and ask dumb questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Think ahead to understand the way forward; ask yourself dumb questions to understand the way before.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use simple, clarifying questions to reveal the structure of a direction or problem; planning helps orient research choices and prevents getting stuck.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attend talks and conferences broadly
rubrics_metrics.description: Attend talks and conferences, even those not directly related to your own work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exposure to diverse topics broadens perspective, can spark new ideas, and helps networking; treat attendance as a learning and community activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Talk to your advisor but take initiative
rubrics_metrics.description: Talk to your advisor, but also take the initiative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use advisor guidance while proactively proposing directions, scheduling meetings, and driving your own projects rather than waiting passively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid premature obsession on a single big problem
rubrics_metrics.description: Don’t prematurely obsess on a single 'big problem' or 'big theory'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early-career focus should include exploring multiple problems/approaches rather than fixating on one grand goal which may be inefficient or premature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write down your work and make it available
rubrics_metrics.description: Write down what you’ve done, and make your work available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep written records of results and circulate drafts; see related advice on how to write and submit papers (publishing and preprints) to increase visibility and feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learn and relearn your field; learn outside your field
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn and relearn your field, but don’t be afraid to learn things outside your field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continually refresh core knowledge while acquiring cross-field tools that can open new problems or techniques; avoid intellectual stagnation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know limitations of your tools and others' strengths
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn the limitations of your tools, but also learn the power of other mathematician’s tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware what methods can and cannot do; study others’ methods to expand your problem-solving arsenal and collaborate effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be flexible and patient in research
rubrics_metrics.description: In your research, you should be both flexible and patient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept that projects evolve, setbacks occur, and progress may be slow; adapt plans and be persistent without forcing unproductive directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel and present research when possible
rubrics_metrics.description: You should definitely travel and present your research if given the opportunity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presentations increase visibility, provide feedback, and build networks; weigh travel benefits against other obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be considerate of your audience — talks differ from papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Be considerate of your audience; talks are not the same as papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust content, level, and exposition for talks versus written papers; prioritize clarity and accessibility in presentations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be sceptical of your own work and discard when necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Be sceptical of your own work, and don’t be afraid to use the wastebasket.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critically evaluate and be willing to abandon flawed approaches or write-ups rather than invest further in dead ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not base career decisions on glamour or fame
rubrics_metrics.description: Don’t base career decisions on glamour or fame.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make choices based on fit, mentorship, training opportunities, and long-term goals rather than perceived prestige alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study at different places
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experience varied institutions/environments to gain broader training, perspectives, and networks; avoid narrowly localizing your early training.

rubrics_metrics.name: There is more to mathematics than grades, exams, methods, rigour, and proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: Note that there is more to maths than grades and exams and methods; there is also more to maths than rigour and proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value intuition, problem selection, communication, conceptual understanding, and creativity in addition to formal correctness and grades.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek stage-specific resources and perspectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Advice is arranged by stage (primary school, high school, undergraduate, graduate, postdoc) and links to additional resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult stage-appropriate materials (e.g., gifted-education advice, competition advice, undergraduate problem-solving guidance, writing/submission advice, and external essays/books linked on the page) for more detailed guidance.
